title: What We Look For Before We Say Yes
seoTitle: What We Look For Before We Say Yes | Evolve VC
description: What Evolve Venture Capital actually looks for before investing: the founding team, evidence behind the story, the Singapore-India market case, and whether we can genuinely help.
excerpt: A good pitch earns a second meeting. Here is what actually earns a term sheet, from the team behind the idea to whether we can genuinely help.
body:
Every founder who pitches us has a good story. Good stories are not rare. What is rare is a founder who can show us, not just tell us, that the story holds up under pressure. Before we say yes to an investment, here is what we are actually looking at.

The Team Behind the Idea

We spend more time on the people than on the slide deck. An idea can pivot; a founding team's judgement, under stress, usually cannot be taught in six weeks. We look for founders who understand their market from the inside, who have already done the unglamorous work of talking to real customers, and who can describe their biggest mistake so far without flinching. How a founder talks about what went wrong tells us more than how they talk about what went right.

We also look at how the founding team works together. Disagreement is healthy. Founders who cannot disagree productively in a pitch meeting rarely do it well when the pressure is higher.

Evidence, Not Just a Story

A compelling narrative earns a second meeting. It does not earn a term sheet. Between the first and second conversation, we are looking for evidence: real usage, a customer who will take a reference call, a pattern in the numbers that holds up when we ask to see the raw data behind them. Founders who are transparent about where the evidence is thin build more trust with us than founders who paper over the gaps.

This is also where our due diligence process earns its keep. We are not trying to catch founders out — we are trying to understand the business as clearly as the founder does, so that when we back it, we are backing it with our eyes open.

A Market Worth Building In

We invest across Singapore, India and the wider Southeast Asia corridor because we believe the next category-defining companies will be built at that intersection, not despite it. So we ask founders a simple question: why does this company need to exist in this region, now? A good answer connects the market opportunity to something structural — a shift in regulation, in technology, or in how customers behave — rather than to a trend that happens to be popular this year.

Whether We Can Actually Help

The last question we ask is about us, not the founder. Capital is not the scarce resource for every promising company — the right partner at the right stage often is. Before we commit, we ask honestly whether Evolve's network, our experience across the Singapore–India corridor, and our mentorship programme will genuinely move the needle for this specific company. If the honest answer is no, the best thing we can do for a founder is say so, and point them toward an investor who is a better fit.

None of this is a formula. Every company we back is different, and the weight we give each of these questions shifts with the stage and the sector. But across every deal we have done, these are the four conversations that mattered most before we said yes.
